research_question: On consumed V54 evidence, can binding pending, hypothetical, request, correction, finite-assertion, and execution-prohibition operators to the target mention or clause fix the attributed semantic errors without changing any previously correct target?
architecture_change: V54 used several sentence-wide lexical decisions. V55 keeps V54 frozen, then adds typed operators bound to the focus target's clause/event: local request force, local finite assertion, local pending/hypothetical scope, quoted-target execution prohibition, and correction to a later requested action even across domains.
human_cognitive_rationale: Humans do not normally apply every uncertainty word or request ending in a sentence to every mentioned action. The intervention represents which event an operator modifies before selecting a commitment, rather than asking a larger model to reinterpret the whole sentence.
evidence_boundary: This is development replay on the already consumed independent V54 holdout with frozen V51 outputs. It can reject V55 or authorize construction of a new holdout, but cannot establish fresh generalization or runtime readiness.

target_mention_patterns.gaze.user: (?:会話相手|こちら|こっち|正面|カメラ|目線|私|俺|僕|目)
target_mention_patterns.motion.idle: (?:そのままの姿勢|動かない|動かず|じっと|アイドル|待機)

decision_rule.pass: Only if every gate passes. A pass authorizes a new independent V55 holdout and separate compiler-repair design, not runtime or physical execution.
decision_rule.semantic_regression: Reject V55 immediately; do not trade aggregate gain for a previously correct semantic regression.
decision_rule.other_failure: Reject V55 under this preregistration and do not tune it on the consumed V54 data.
